title: Chapter 22 — The Luxury Brand Landscape and Lead-Time Mastery
intro: The top-tier map, ordering realities, and the lead-time fluency that runs luxury projects.

sections.title: The Luxury Map
sections.content:
The luxury segment has distinct players with different strengths. Some brands dominate in refrigeration. Others in cooking. Others in the full-suite integrated kitchen. Know which brands lead in which categories and what their differentiators are.

Luxury customers and their designers often have brand preferences. Your job is to understand those preferences and either support them with expertise or offer alternatives with honest reasoning.

sections.title: Lead-Time Fluency
sections.content:
Luxury appliances often have lead times measured in months — sometimes six months or more. Lead time is not a problem to apologize for. It is a project reality to manage.

Knowing current lead times by brand and category makes you indispensable to designers and contractors who are planning projects around delivery schedules. If you cannot answer the lead-time question confidently, the designer will find someone who can.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating luxury brand knowledge, ask:

Does the salesperson know the major luxury brands and their category strengths?
Can they quote current lead times accurately?
Do they manage lead-time expectations proactively with customers and project teams?
